analysis.investment_thesis: Greaves Cotton fails virtually every quantitative standard I require — negative earnings in 4 of the last 5 years, a P/E of 34.6 and P/B of 2.67 both far exceeding my thresholds, and free cash flow negative in each of the last four years. A business consuming capital without generating it is not a business — it is a speculation.
key_strengths: Very low financial leverage: Debt/Equity of 0.12 and borrowings of INR 185 Cr against INR 1,376 Cr equity — the balance sheet is not yet impaired by debt
Long operating history since 1859 with an established engines and aftermarket business generating real revenues of INR 2,918 Cr in FY2025
Promoter holding of 55.8% signals owner-operator alignment and skin in the game
key_risks: Earnings record is disqualifying: net losses in FY2021 (−19 Cr), FY2022 (−35 Cr), FY2024 (−367 Cr), and near-zero FY2025 (−6 Cr) — I require at least 5 consecutive years of positive earnings, and this company has not managed even 3
Free cash flow has been negative four consecutive years (−24, −206, −225, −98 Cr) and OCF was positive only once in five years — the business is not self-funding
Operating margin collapsed from 12.6% in FY2016 to 3.94% today; a 9-year negative CAGR of −4.3% in operating income means the core engine of earnings power has been destroyed
red_flags: The INR −367 Cr loss in FY2024 driven by 'Other Income' of −270 Cr almost certainly reflects massive write-downs on Ampere (EV two-wheeler) — capital has been destroyed, not invested
Reserves have eroded from INR 1,540 Cr (FY2023) to INR 1,329 Cr (FY2025) — equity is being consumed, not compounded
P/E of 34.6 is calculated on a razor-thin near-zero profit base; any earnings normalisation reveals the true premium being paid for a structurally weak business
Finance costs growing at a 36.1% CAGR (INR 1 Cr in 2016 → INR 16 Cr in 2025) while earnings collapse — leverage creeping up precisely when it should not
No mention of any meaningful dividend, consistent with cash being consumed rather than returned to shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Greaves Cotton fails my most fundamental test: the requirement for demonstrated, consistent earning power. Of the last nine years, net profit has been negative or near-zero in four — including a catastrophic INR −367 Cr loss in FY2024. The Graham Number is mathematically incalculable for a company with negative or near-nil earnings, which alone tells me everything. A P/B of 2.67 means I am paying 2.67 times the net assets of a business that has been destroying those assets: equity has shrunk from INR 1,587 Cr to INR 1,376 Cr in just two years. At INR 161, Mr. Market is asking me to pay a premium for what are effectively impaired assets.

The EV transition — via the Ampere brand — has been a capital incinerator. Operating cash flow was positive only once in five years, and free cash flow has been negative every year since FY2022, totaling over INR 550 Cr in cumulative cash destruction. The gross margin of 32.69% tells me the underlying products have some pricing power, but an operating margin of only 3.94% means enormous fixed costs, investment losses, and structural inefficiency swallow that gross profit whole. The company's 165-year history earns it no valuation concession from me — I pay for proven, current earning power, not heritage. I would only revisit this stock if it traded below book value (INR ~59 per share based on current equity) with three consecutive years of genuine free cash flow. At INR 161, the margin of safety is negative.
